US stocks edged lower Thursday, snapping a rebound that had lifted the S&P 500 1.3% a day earlier. The S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.36% to 52,297.09, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.39% to 25,366.09, Yahoo Finance reported, as bond yields rose. Traders weighed hot inflation data, the Federal Reserve's next move and higher oil prices.

Hot Inflation Keeps the Fed in Focus

The week's moves have been shaped by interest rates. Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report convinced traders that the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month, Reuters said. According to CME FedWatch, investors fully price in a hike of at least 25 basis points, with a 13.2% chance of a 50-basis-point move. Several Fed officials have said they are open to a more aggressive path, and Wall Street analysts have raised their forecasts for more and bigger hikes, Yahoo Finance said.

Wednesday's rebound showed how quickly sentiment can swing. The S&P 500 gained 1.3% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.6% after results from an AI cloud company eased worries about the durability of the artificial intelligence trade, Reutersreported, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners by 1.3 to 1 on the NYSE. The Treasury market was closed for Veterans Day, so bond traders could react only on Thursday.

Oil Adds to the Uncertainty

Thursday brought another pressure point. Oil prices climbed after the president said he was no longer interested in a deal with Iran, the Associated Press reported, which complicates the inflation outlook. Higher energy costs feed into the same inflation numbers the Fed is fighting. Even so, the S&P 500 finished with a modest loss and is up 2.9% for the week.

Retail investors are watching the same swings closely, and Reddit threads tend to cluster around names where the gap between price and analyst expectations looks widest. That gap deserves some care. An average price target is a twelve-month estimate pulled from sell-side analysts, it is often revised after earnings, and a handful of outliers can skew the mean. Because upside is measured against the current share price, a sharp drop widens it overnight, while a rally shrinks it just as fast. Readers who follow that chatter can browse our list of undervalued stocks to buy according to Reddit. You may also want to read our ranking of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50%-plus upside.

With inflation, the Fed and AI spending all in play, the stocks below sit where the debate is loudest, and each one carries an average analyst target well above its recent price.

Stocks fell in shaky trading on Wall Street Friday, but the market still posted its first winning week since early October.

The S&P 500 fell 0.4% Friday and closed with a weekly gain of 2.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 50 points, or 0.1%. The Nasdaq composite fell 0.9%.

title: Sell Alert: 5 Stocks Analysts Downgraded on Wednesday
detail:
Sell Alert: 5 Stocks Analysts Downgraded on Wednesday
Farooq

CL=F
^DJI
HALO
Trade HALO on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Wall Street got a sharp reminder this month of how fast sentiment can turn. Last Thursday the S&P 500 lost 4.4%, its worst day since April 2025, after midterm election results raised fears that regulation could hurt the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite fell into correction territory, roughly 11% below the record it set in early October.

A rally on lower oil prices offered some relief at the start of this week. Then inflation data reopened the wound. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, the third straight monthly gain of at least that size and a touch above the 0.3% economists had expected. The stock market was still nervous from the prior week's rout, and it showed. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93, the Dow lost 0.30% and the Nasdaq Composite slid 0.74% on the news.

Inflation Revives Talk of Fed Rate Hikes

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise interest rates in December and consider a half-point increase if inflation worsens. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan went further, saying at least two more quarter-point hikes are needed to bring prices under control. Three straight monthly gains of 0.4% or more is the kind of streak that keeps rate-hike talk alive.

Traders have taken the message seriously. They now price roughly an 84% chance of a quarter-point December hike, after a week in which both the stock and bond markets swung hard.

Investors tracking how far some AI stocks have fallen can find more names in our ranking of oversold AI stocks that analysts see rebounding by more than half.

Chip Stocks Absorb the Heaviest Selling

Technology shares have taken the brunt of it. Selling in semiconductor stocks reached its most extreme level since 2019 earlier this week, by Yahoo Finance's measure, as worries about regulation of the AI trade added to the pressure.

Wednesday brought a rebound. The S&P 500 climbed 1.31% to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.60%, and the Dow rose 0.49%. The Nasdaq Composite had slipped into correction territory only days earlier. One day of gains does not erase the damage from the prior week, and the inflation and rate questions behind the selloff are still open. The Dow finished the day at 52,486.49.

Investors comparing cheaper alternatives can start with our roundup of affordable stocks that Wall Street analysts favor.

For now, the Federal Reserve's December meeting is the date traders are watching, with a hike priced as the likely outcome.

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stock Preachers News Commentary - Wall Street closed out a volatile week with every major index still higher versus last Friday, even after a broad Friday retreat. The Nasdaq Composite led decliners with a 1.24% drop on the session, while the S&P 500 fell 0.75% and the Dow slipped 0.14%. For the week, the S&P 500 gained 2.15%, the Nasdaq rose 1.92% and the Dow added 1.83%, as chip-driven strength carried the market even as Friday gave back some ground heading into the weekend. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY), vVardis (NYSE: VVVV), NVIDIA Corporation (Nasdaq: NVDA), Caterpillar Inc. (NYSE: CAT), and Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC).

Stock Preachers Logo

The S&P 500 closed at 7535.72, down 56.68 points on the day but up 158.86 points, or 2.15%, from last Friday's 7376.86 close. The index touched a week high of 7652.76 and a week low of 7422.24, and sits up 10.08% year to date. Its RSI14 reading of 45.6 points to a market that cooled off from overbought conditions during the week.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 315.80 points, or 1.24%, on Friday to 25050.29, trimming its weekly gain to 1.92% from the November 6 close of 24579.43. The index ranged between 24762.57 and 25649.85 during the week and carries an RSI14 of 41.6, the weakest among major indices. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 75.29 points to 52221.80, still up 1.83% on the week and 8.65% year to date, while the Russell 2000 eased 17.98 points to 2781.08, up 0.98% for the week.

The VIX rose 1.14 points to 19.84 on Friday, essentially flat on the week, while the VXN volatility gauge climbed 1.33 points to 29.88 but ended the week down 4.14 points. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3 basis points on the day and 27 basis points on the week to 5.13%. Gold fell 5.56% for the week to $3,885.70 an ounce, silver dropped 6.66% to $49.06, and WTI crude added 1.92% to $88.52 a barrel.
